Sending Through the Email Listener

notifyEmail.listener.js: the same domainEvents.on() shape as the in-app channel, calling transport.sendMail() instead of prisma.notification.create().

// Figure 5.12: the email channel's take on ticket.created (src/events/listeners/notifyEmail.listener.js, excerpt)
domainEvents.on(EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, async (ticket) => {
  try {
    await mailer.sendMail({
      from: env.MAIL_FROM,
      to: ticket.customer.email,
      subject: `Ticket #${ticket.id} created: ${ticket.subject}`,
      text: `Hi ${ticket.customer.name},\n\nWe've received your ticket and an agent will respond shortly.`,
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('notifyEmail listener failed for ticket.created:', err);
  }
});

Nothing here is new mechanism — it's the previous topic's domainEvents.on(...) pattern and try/catch discipline, reacting to the same ticket.created event notifyInApp.listener.js already reacted to, in a completely separate file that has no idea the other one exists. ticket.customer.email and ticket.customer.name are only available here because createTicket included customer in the payload it emitted (Topic 3) — this listener never queries Prisma itself.

The remaining three events follow the same shape: ticket.assigned emails ticket.assignedAgent, ticket.commented loops over the resolved recipients and sends one email each (via Promise.all, so they go out concurrently rather than one at a time), and ticket.status_changed emails the customer with previousStatus and the new one in the message. Four events, three listener files, twelve domainEvents.on(...) blocks in total — and not one of them calls another.
